text:
jess: noticed a 20-30% jump in cost-per-token for the last deploy window, digging in. dashboard shows kernel-stage latency up across several routes :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
arthur: which deploy? commit or PR id?
jess: rolled kernel selector change (PR #2287) at ~1839900000, commit 6f3a8b2. also a small batching tweak in the async-batcher.
jess: posting the prom sample I grabbed from last hour:
```
redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/api/generate",stage="kernel",kernel="generic"} 0.012
redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/api/generate",stage="kernel",kernel="optimized_v2"} 0.030
redwood_kv_cache_miss_count{route="/api/generate"} 452
redwood_batch_size_histogram{route="/api/generate"} 1 1 2 4 8
```
jess: note the `optimized_v2` kernel showing much higher latency on long sequences, and kv misses spiked.
maria: the per-route KPI tile shows /chat-highmem latency p95 up 40%, cost/unit also up. do we have kernel tag on token metrics? not currently, we only have stage and route. we should add `kernel_type` to token-level histogram.
nash: (cc @ash) any profiling from the GPU side?
ash is a typo; ash: I pulled a quick nvprof profile on a repro run, looks like kernel launch overhead + memcpy increased for optimized_v2 on batch sizes <=4. snippet:
```
# nvprof summary
Kernel: attn_forward_v2  time 54.3ms calls 1
Memcpy HtoD  2.1ms calls 8
Kernel launch overhead ~ 1.8ms per call (small kernels)
```
ash: oops ignore, meant @ash.
arthur: if small batches cause lots of kernel launches, selector might be choosing optimized_v2 for cases it's not suitable for. batching heuristic change could be sending smaller micro-batches.
jess: agree. immediate mitigation: revert kernel selector to v1 for the next canary and pin `kernel_selector: v1` in route config for /chat-highmem.
billing-bot: alert — cost-per-token anomaly detected for service=hosted-api; delta +27% last 60m, projected $14k extra/mo at current rate. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sre-bot: deploy revert job queued by jess, will run canary in 2m.
arthur: long-term: we need a metric that joins kernel selection + batch-size + kv-miss to the token latency so we can build a per-route cost model. add `kernel_type`, `batch_bucket`, `kv_miss_rate` labels to the token latency histogram if feasible.
maria: I can add a dashboard tile with a stacked breakdown by `kernel_type` and a delta panel for cost-per-token. also add an alert if kernel-specific p95 increases by >20%.
jess: did the canary revert — quick numbers after revert (5m): p95 kernel latency down ~12%, cost-per-token trending back toward baseline.
arthur: great. opened issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4492 "kernel selector: add safety guards + telemetry" and assigned to @ash and @jess.
maria: tagging analytics to reconcile billing accounting vs prometheus token accounting as well.
jess: follow-up tasks: 1) add kernel_type label to token histograms 2) add per-route delta tile for cost-per-token 3) add canary gating for kernel selector PRs 4) run a KV cache hotkey analysis (why misses spiked).
ash: typo again, meant @ash — I'll own the KV cache hotkey analysis, will post results tomorrow.
sre-bot: deploy revert completed by jess — canary OK :white_check_mark:.
jess: thanks all, keeping the thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
